children: BlackRock (BLK, Financials), is getting closer to a potentially massive data-center deal as a consortium backed by the asset manager and IFM Investors enters exclusive talks to acquire Stack Infrastructure's Asia-Pacific portfolio for up to $25 billion, Bloomberg News reported.

The group includes BlackRock-backed Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Partnership (AIP) and IFM. It is preparing to conduct due diligence on the assets and hopes to reach an agreement soon with Stack owner Blue Owl Capital, according to the report.
The potential transaction comes as investors pour billions into data centers to meet rising demand for cloud computing, artificial intelligence and digital services.

Stack operates facilities across major Asia-Pacific markets, including Tokyo, Osaka, Sydney and Melbourne. Bloomberg previously reported in May that Stack was considering a sale of its Asia operations at a valuation above $30 billion.

The deal is not yet done. Reuters said the talks remain ongoing and could be extended or fail to produce an agreement. BlackRock, IFM, Stack and AIP did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

AIP launched in late 2024 with plans to initially invest more than $30 billion in AI-related infrastructure, including data centers and energy facilities. Nvidia, Microsoft, xAI and MGX are among its investors.
The next catalyst is whether due diligence leads to a definitive agreement and what valuation the parties ultimately place on Stack's Asia-Pacific assets.

title: BlackRock Just Made a $25 Billion Bet on Asia's AI Data Centers
